thread:
incident-bot: Paging oncall — Dedicated pool 'eu-west-2-prod-io' is reporting sustained queue depth > 95% for the past 6m. Possible autoscale lag.
Alex: I'm seeing a spike from a handful of customers, looks like a traffic burst from Acme Corp. Token rates jumped ~6x.
Maya: Confirmed. Metrics: 120s p90 latency up from 140ms -> 1.2s, error rate creeping to 1.6%.
Jun: Is autoscaler healthy? Any failed scale events?
Alex: Checking autoscaler logs now — a couple of failed node provisioning events around 00:14UTC, then backoff. Looks like we hit provider quota for inline GPUs.
Lucy: FYI Acme support pinged us saying their background batch ran unexpectedly and they're seeing timeouts. Jordan (Acme) is in thread.
Jordan (Acme): yep — we accidentally left a ramp in our job. We're throttling from our side now, sorry. Can you do anything to keep us online while we fix?
Maya: We need quick mitigations: 1) enable Dedicated pool burst capacity if available, 2) apply temporary per-customer rate limit, 3) disable non-essential features (reranking) for impacted pool. Suggest order: burst toggle -> per-cust cap -> feature disable. Thoughts?
Jun: Agree. Burst toggle first to buy time. If provider quota prevents scaling, burst is our only short-term option.
Alex: I have console access. Preparing commands.
Alex: (action) Enabling burst capacity for pool eu-west-2-prod-io, target+burst=+40% for 15m, notify.
Alex: Command I ran: ```
# enable burst
curl -X POST "https://console.redwood.internal/api/dedicated/pools/eu-west-2-prod-io/burst" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer RESTRICTED_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"enable":true,"burst_pct":40,"duration_min":15}'
```
incident-bot: Action recorded: burst capacity ENABLED on eu-west-2-prod-io by Alex at 00:18UTC.
Maya: Good. Next, let's set a soft per-customer cap for Acme while they finish. Apply a 3x/sec per-key token limit and drop long-run jobs to background.
Jun: We can patch routing policy to mark Acme requests as rate_limited: true and set quota to 3rps. I'll push a canary rule.
Jun: Patch snippet: ```
# routing policy patch
PATCH /routing/policies/put
{
  "match": {"customer_id":"acme"},
  "actions": [{"type":"set_rate_limit","rps":3},{"type":"bypass_reranking"}]
}
```
incident-bot: Routing policy change applied (canary) to 10% of traffic for acme by Jun.
Alex: Also toggled reranking off for the impacted pool to reduce per-request cost. Command: `adminctl feature-toggle set --pool eu-west-2-prod-io --feature reranking --state off`
Maya: Monitoring after burst + canary cap + reranking off. Immediate signals: queue depth down to 60% in 2m, p90 latency 300ms, errors back to 0.4%. Good.
Jordan (Acme): we reduced our job concurrency and paused the batch. Seeing improvements from our end too. Thanks.
Lucy: Customer impact summary for postmortem: Acme traffic spike caused autoscaler to hit provider quota which prevented node provisioning; resulted in degraded latency and ~1.6% errors across the pool for ~12 minutes. Mitigations: burst capacity enabled (+40% for 15m), per-customer canary rate cap (3rps), reranking disabled on pool. No data loss, some requests timed out and were retried.
Maya: Can we add a short-term billing note for Acme about accidental burst? Also follow up: request cloud quota increase and add a provider-quotas alert to oncall runbooks.
Alex: Filing follow-ups: 1) Support ticket to Acme about best practices for background jobs and client-side backoff. 2) Infra ticket to request GPU quota bump in eu-west-2. 3) Runbook add: when autoscaler fails to provision for >=2 attempts, auto-enable burst (with guardrails).
Jun: I'll create a small automation to auto-enable burst for 10 minutes if queue_depth > 90% and scale_failure_count >= 2. Will draft in eng-platform.
incident-bot: Note: oncall handoff in 50m — @Maya will hand to @Alex.
Maya: I'll start the handoff doc now, will include timeline and commands run.
Alex: I'll keep watch for the remaining 10m of burst window and the canary rollout, then revert reranking once stable.
Lucy: Marking incident as mitigated for customer-facing comms. Assigning postmortem owner: Maya.
Jordan (Acme): Appreciate the quick help. We'll add client-side safeguards.
Maya: TL;DR — root cause: unexpected customer batch + provider quota -> autoscale failure. Short term: burst toggle + per-customer cap + feature disable. Long term: quota increase, runbook automation, and customer guidance.
Alex: Closing thread after handoff. If anything regresses ping in #eng-oncall. :thumbsup:
